games.blurb: A 37-point beatdown and the second-highest score in the league. Amon-Ra St. Brown (28.7) did Amon-Ra things, and Etienne got contributions up and down the lineup. William's Wild Team put up a respectable 125 — a number that beats four other teams this week — and it still didn't matter even a little. Sometimes you draw the buzzsaw.

Justin Jefferson (31.2) and Josh Allen (**35.66, the top starter in the entire league**) is a rough combo to stare across at on a Sunday. **Cash Money 8 Ballers** have grievances to file, though: they nailed the **#1 overall pick on Jahmyr Gibbs (33.6)** and _still_ lost by 30 — because their **3rd-round tight end Brock Bowers put up a clean 0.0.** Zero. Nothing. A round-3 goose egg. Gibbs can't do it alone, fellas.

**Game of the week** — the only matchup decided by fewer than 30 points (margin 14). Two middling scores, but actual drama, and it came right down to the wire. Dirty Danglers survived despite **2nd-round pick A.J. Brown mustering just 5.6**, which tells you they had just enough everywhere else. In Tua We Trust will feel this one — a few more points from any bench spot and they steal it.

Okay. Deep breath. **Ignorance is Vid's started Kyler Murray at quarterback and he scored NEGATIVE 0.38 points.** Your QB was a _net drain_ on the roster. On the bench, gathering dust: **Christian Watson (32.7) and DJ Moore (21)** — that's 90.1 points of bench, more than **Sausage Party's entire starting lineup managed (75).** And Vid's won anyway. **Luckiest winner of the week,** and honestly the luckiest man alive. Sausage Party, for the record, just got quietly outscored across the board — a clean, honest loss, no notes, better luck next week.

Highest score of the week, and Kenney Powers earned it: Jaxon Smith-Njigba (26.2) balled out and the whole roster showed up. Spare a thought for **Greasy Hucksters**, though — they dropped 130 points, a total that wins in most weeks, and got run off the field anyway. The kicker: they used the **8th overall pick on Ja'Marr Chase, who managed 3.2 points.** You scored 130 _without your best player._ That's either terrifying or heartbreaking, and this week it was heartbreaking. **Unluckiest loser of Week 1.**

**Blowout of the week (margin 51.6),** and yet Chimere is who this recap really wants to talk about. Kenneth Walker III went nuclear (34.1) and Chuba Hubbard (23.7) chipped in — but sitting on Chimere's **bench was Caleb Williams and his 37.26 points, the single highest score by anyone in the entire league.** You benched the week's best player and still won by 51. That's not a flex, that's a warning shot to the rest of the league. Meanwhile **Bullpuckey Music for Idiots** scored **68.8** — the low mark of the week by 34 points — and we may need to organize a search party.

weeks.intro:
What's up my sons my name is Tomas and I am your commissioner this season of fantasy football. My plan is to do a little recap each week to keep things interesting throughout the season. In the future I'll try to be a bit quicker on getting it done by Thursday.
Anyways we had a pretty interesting first week of fantasy. We have a team whose QB scored negative points and still won, a first-round WR who did fuck all, and a bench that might've been able to beat half the league.

games.blurb: **William's Wild Team gets their first W of the season** and did it the absolute hardest way by starting an injured **Puka Nacua**. Trey McBride (18.1) and Joe Burrow (16.2) had respectable games while Tre Tucker popped off on the bench (btw are the Raiders good??). This game really belongs to the ongoing tragedy that is **Cash Money 8 Ballers**, now **0-2 despite rostering Patrick Mahomes (28.98) AND Jahmyr Gibbs (23.3).** How do you lose with that? By insisting on starting a Titans WR over **Jalen Coker (14.6), Rachaad White (14.3), and Romeo Doubs (12.6)**. This was such a winnable game for Cash Money 8 Ballers. We'll see if they adjust their lineup for the next week.

**Etienne This D quietly moves to 2-0** and barely broke a sweat. Amon-Ra St. Brown went for **35.2**, Brandon Aubrey the _GOAT kicker_ put up **17**, and they _still_ stranded a league-high **68.78 on the bench**. For Eitenne This D, consistency will be king. **Dirty Danglers** finally got their receivers going — Olave (22.6) and Waddle (21.8) — but Colston Loveland handed them another **1.3 at tight end**, and that position remains this franchise's personal hell. Danglers is going to be hoping that their first round pick in Bijan steps up to his role if they're going to hope for a win.

I'm sure Ima B.U.S.T. characteristically busted over **Josh Allen's 40.82 points.** And although many players on the team had stinkers, Kyren Williams, Tyler Warren, and Harrison Butker (ofc) carried B.U.S.T to the **Blowout of the week with a margin of 41.** **Sausage Party** takes home **Biggest Loser** at **86.98** and drops to **0-2**. They are going to really want Jameson Williams to get involved with the Lions offense. And they have a big question, is Malik Nabers JameisWinston-proof? We'll find out next time if Sasuage Party can finally eclipse 100 points.

Redemption for **Ja'Marr Chase**, who followed up his 3.2-point no-show with a respectable **26.5**. Greasy needed it too, because not only did they forget to bench an injured Zay Flowers, but they also started Justin Herbert who had an absolute stinker. WTF is going on with the Chargers? **My Penix is Rising/In Tua We Trust** falls to **0-2** with a rough starting lineup. He matched a 0 point WR with a 0 point WR with a sluggish Marvin Harrison Jr. who looks like he's forgotten how to run routes. Meanwhile Denzel Boston (who??) and Bryce Young sat on the bench, both with huge numbers. Maybe next week this team can put their best players forward for the first W of the season.

**Nailbiter of the week with 0.64 points margin.** And oh, it stings. **Ignorance is Vid's** did have points on the bench that would have won the match-up. And DJ Moore went out early after a shoulder injury in a game where his QB put up a NVP performance. Sigh. Vid's went from last week's luckiest winner to this week's most excruciating loser. **Bullpuckey Music for Idiots** who looked dead to rights for the season last week will gladly take it, powered by **CeeDee Lamb (35.3)** and **Jake Ferguson (20.3)** even though **Saquon Barkley gave them only 3** (although I think he was injured?). Either way, a win's a win. Welcome to the middle of the pack.

Top score of the week and, yeah, it's me again. After I wrongly benched Caleb Williams last week, he went and got himself injured after I started him (should have kept him on the bench bc of the weather anyway). But my GOAT Davante Adams saved my life. Spare a thought for **Kenney Powers**, though. We've all been there. The league-best and actual GOAT **Jaxon Smith-Njigba** put up the most points by any player and the GOAT of yesteryear **Stefan Diggs** turned back the clock. With **147.96** Kenny Powers is our **Unluckiest loser of the week** with a points total that would have beaten any other team this week.

weeks.intro: What's up my sons, back again with your Week 2 recap. Yeah this is even later than last week but what are you gonna do. This was the week of the bench quarterback. Half of you (including me) sat a QB who popped off and started some guy who did nothing (or got injured in the first half). We've got three teams still undefeated, a matchup decided by **0.64 points**, and Josh Allen once again playing a different sport than the rest of us.
